script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Comedy
Theme: second chances

Begin screenplay.

Title: Fresh Start Café

INT. FRESH START CAFÉ - DAY

A warm, cozy café, filled with the sweet scent of freshly brewed coffee. Customers chat and laugh as they sip their drinks.

Behind the counter, JANE, 30s, a kind and compassionate woman, prepares orders with a smile. Her assistant, MIKE, early 20s, a quirky and energetic guy, helps out.

JANE
(to Mike)
You're really growing on me, Mike.

MIKE
(laughs)
You say that every day, Jane. But it's a good thing, right?

Jane nods, her expression thoughtful.

INT. FRESH START CAFÉ - KITCHEN - LATER

Jane and Mike work on a new dish for the café: avocado toast with poached eggs and bacon.

MIKE
So, why'd you start this café, Jane?

JANE
(pauses, reflecting)
I wanted to create a place where people could come for a fresh start. A place where they could relax, be themselves, and maybe even find a new opportunity.

MIKE
(smiling)
Like us?

JANE
(laughs)
Exactly like us.

EXT. CITY PARK - DAY

A group of people, all with troubled pasts, sit together on the grass, enjoying their café treats. They share stories and laughs, looking happier than they have in a long time.

INT. FRESH START CAFÉ - DAY

The bell above the door rings as RACHEL, a young woman in her late twenties, enters. She looks nervous and unsure.

RACHEL
(to Jane)
I saw your café online. I thought... I needed a fresh start.

JANE
(smiling warmly)
You're in the right place, Rachel.

INT. FRESH START CAFÉ - KITCHEN - LATER

Jane and Mike prepare another round of orders as the café buzzes with activity.

MIKE
You know, Jane, I think this café is doing more than just serving coffee. It's giving people a second chance at life.

JANE
(smiling)
That's the idea, Mike. And it's all thanks to you and our wonderful customers.

INT. FRESH START CAFÉ - EVENING

The café closes for the day, and Jane and Mike tidy up.

MIKE
Another successful day, Jane. I'm proud to be a part of this.

JANE
(smiling)
And I'm proud to have you, Mike.

They share a warm, genuine smile as they lock up and head home, ready to face another day at the Fresh Start Café.

FADE OUT.
